claim.why_it_matters: The header/delimiter rows declare 5 columns but the sub-header row supplies 6 cells. Under CommonMark/GFM table rules cells beyond the declared column count are discarded, so the ')' column header disappears from the rendered table, and the continuation rows on page 206 (written as a separate 6-column table) no longer line up with this header.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, and the failure mode was reproduced rather than assumed. PDF (E:/Temp/specrecon/v205/spec_p205.png, 300 dpi, cropped to the table): Table 3 is a SIX-column table. The leftmost column is the corner/stub header 'First symbol' (spanning both header rows); 'Second symbol' spans the remaining five columns above the second header row; the five sub-headers read, left to right, 'Identifier or literal', '+ – * / **', 'Unary + or –', '(' and ')'. The '(' and ')' columns are visibly narrow but are genuinely two distinct ruled columns with their own vertical rule between them — I read the printed glyphs directly and there is a '(' cell and a separate ')' cell. The claim's description of the PDF is exact. Markdown (E:/Temp/specrecon/v205/page-205.md lines 43-45): mechanically counting pipe-delimited cells gives line 43 = 5 cells ['First symbol', 'Second symbol', '', '', ''], line 44 (delimiter) = 5, line 45 = 6 cells ['', '**Identifier or literal**', '**+ – * / \*\***', '**Unary + or –**', '**(**', '**)**']. The claim quotes both rows verbatim; the en-dashes are genuine U+2013 (no encoding damage), so the only defect is the column count. The claim misquotes neither source. Rendering check (markdown-it, commonmark preset + table plugin, run on the exact fragment): the emitted HTML is a 5-column table whose only body row ends at '('. The ')' cell is silently discarded, exactly as GFM specifies ('if a row has greater [cells than the header row], the excess is ignored'). So this is not merely cosmetic whitespace — a real column header is lost on render. This is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation: the whole header block sits on page 205 and the loss is structural. Refutation attempted and failed — the ')' text does survive in the raw source bytes, but it is unreachable through any table-aware consumer, which is the entire purpose of transcribing it as a table. Confirmed real.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with two refinements to the original write-up. (1) The mechanism is precisely as claimed and was reproduced: header row = 5 cells, delimiter row = 5 cells, sub-header row = 6 cells; markdown-it renders a 5-column table ending at '(', dropping '**)**' entirely. The transcription should declare SIX columns (delimiter '|---|---|---|---|---|---|'), with the header row carrying the stub 'First symbol' plus the five 'Second symbol' sub-headers, and the 'Second symbol' spanner recorded as a note or an explicit second header line, since markdown tables cannot express the PDF's two-level spanning header. (2) The page-206 half has an additional, distinct defect the claim only gestures at: E:/Temp/specrecon/v206/page-206.md lines 6-7 make the FIRST data row of the continuation ('| Identifier or literal | — | P | — | — | P |') serve as that table's header row, so besides being orphaned from the page-205 header, the 'Identifier or literal' row is rendered as column headings rather than as data. The two fragments should be reunited into one 6-column table spanning the page boundary. The normative content — the P / — permissibility matrix itself — is intact and unaltered on both pages, so 'cosmetic' remains the right severity.
